solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Environment with kangaroo, one that just looks

parts.note: Windows is Microsoft's operating environment for PCs
a kangaroo is a hopper, an animal that moves by hopping

explanation.surface: A zoo-like scene: a habitat with a kangaroo and a visitor who merely gazes at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Environment' reads as natural habitat, but it is the computing sense: Windows, the operating environment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone browsing shop displays without buying is one who merely looks at the goods.

clue.text: Drink concoction of snow-white sleet

indicators.note: a concoction is something mixed up, so the letters of the following words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A wintry cocktail made from pure white sleet.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to have a drink, moistening the throat that whistles.

clue.text: Neuter or masculine? Singular standards needed

parts.note: N is the grammatical abbreviation for neuter
M is the grammatical abbreviation for masculine
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A grammar question about noun genders, then a note that singular forms are the norm.
explanation.definitionFit: Accepted standards of behaviour or quality are the usual patterns expected, synonyms here.

clue.text: Frequently concerning decimal table

parts.note: of can mean about or concerning, as in 'tales of adventure'
the ten times table is the multiplication table based on ten, hence decimal

explanation.surface: A remark on how often one consults the table of tens.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned adverb meaning often, on many occasions — a direct synonym.

clue.text: Weep at dawn, not acting at first in a restrained manner

parts.note: to sob is to weep noisily

indicators.note: not tells us to take a letter away from the word before it

parts.note: early means at the start of the day, at dawn

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word acting

explanation.surface: Someone crying at daybreak, not putting it on, yet staying composed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not acting at first' removes A, the first letter of 'acting', from EARLY to leave ERLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting soberly means behaving with calm self-control, a restrained manner.

clue.text: Perform in theatre as Figaro, perhaps reaching lower note

indicators.note: in a down entry the note sits lower, coming after the first piece

parts.note: The Marriage of Figaro is an example of an opera
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A singer performs on stage as Figaro, stretching for a low note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests the stage, but it is the operating theatre where surgeons work.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons carry out procedures in the operating theatre, so to perform there is to do surgery.

clue.text: Work up representative ceremony

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

explanation.surface: An elected representative works up a formal ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremony and splendid display are synonyms for formal show and pageantry.

clue.text: In Perth headmaster has no alternative: if that is resistance, one delivers correction

indicators.note: has no tells us to drop the following letters from the headmaster

parts.note: in Scotland (Perth is a Scottish city) a school's head is called a rector
or introduces an alternative
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A Scottish head teacher, with no other option, is the one who administers correction.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectifier is a device or person that puts things right; in electronics it corrects alternating current to direct.

clue.text: Old pine carried by the cog

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it
something carried by a vehicle is in it
a cog is a tooth on a gear wheel

explanation.surface: A pine log being carried along by a toothed wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like the tree, but it is the verb meaning to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone getting on in years, from ageing horses' receding gums.

clue.text: One goes round in time with altar vessel to be stored

indicators.note: in, together with to be stored, places one piece inside the other
something stored is kept inside, so the vessel goes within the other letters

parts.note: the communion table in a church is the altar
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A church scene: a vessel to be kept on the altar, with something spinning in time.
explanation.definitionFit: A record deck's rotating platter is one thing that goes round and round.

clue.text: Scot goes to house of aggressive male

parts.note: Mac is an informal name for a Scotsman

explanation.surface: A Scotsman heads to the home of a tough guy.
explanation.definitionFit: A swaggering he-man who displays exaggerated masculinity and aggression is described this way.

clue.text: Car appears half-hearted this month

indicators.note: the heart of the car name is a doubled letter; losing half of it leaves one

parts.note: Nissan is a Japanese car maker

explanation.surface: A car seems lacklustre this month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this month' must be read as the answer itself being a month: it is in the Hebrew calendar, around March–April.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the first month of the Jewish religious year, when Passover falls.

clue.text: Cancel scrapping exercise material

indicators.note: scrapping tells us to discard the following letters

parts.note: to repeal a law is to cancel it
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A decision to stop scrapping cloth used for exercise wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' suggests cloth; here it is the adjective meaning physical, actual.
explanation.definitionFit: Material things are tangible and actual, existing rather than imagined.

clue.text: Heath inhabitant rambling? Not half

indicators.note: not half means the first half of the word rambling is dropped

explanation.surface: Something living on a heath: is it wandering? Not much.
explanation.definitionFit: This is another name for common heather, a plant growing on heathland.

clue.text: Programme to care after teacher

indicators.note: after places the word for care behind the word for teacher

parts.note: a schoolmaster is a teacher
to mind is to care, as in 'I don't mind'

explanation.surface: A schedule for looking after the teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running BBC television quiz with the famous black chair is this programme.

clue.text: Mark provided variable scratch

parts.note: a scar is a mark on the skin
if means provided that
y is a typical algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A mark left if some variable scratch occurs.
explanation.definitionFit: To score or scratch the surface of skin or soil is a synonym.

clue.text: Signature dish of ragout served by a pub

indicators.note: to dish something is to ruin it, so the letters of ragout are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: PH is public house, a pub

explanation.surface: A chef's signature dish of stew served in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signature dish' reads as one phrase, but 'Signature' is the definition and 'dish of' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's handwritten name, as given to a fan, is their signature.

clue.text: Girl's one close to attempt to escape

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name; with the 's it gives Eva's
I is the Roman numeral one
on can mean near or next to, as in a town on the coast

explanation.surface: A girl's single nearby try at getting away.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodging or avoiding something, as in escaping a question, is a synonym for this.

clue.text: Fired first to end worry in difficult position

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved to the end of the word

parts.note: a gun fired has shot
to eat at someone is to worry them, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: A sacked person's first concern is ending up in a tough spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being put on the spot under pressure, like a quiz contestant, is an idiomatic difficult position.

clue.text: One is of note being raised in country

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a means one
in can stand for of, as in 'one in a million'
ut is the old name for the note now called doh

explanation.surface: A person of note being promoted in their country.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African nation whose capital is Tunis is a country.

clue.text: Sailor in vehicle's hot and cold

indicators.note: in places the sailor inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle; the 's means 'is' as a link
a tar is a sailor
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A sailor sitting in his car is alternately hot and cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot and cold' reads as one phrase but splits: H, then 'cold' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A head cold brings mucus inflammation of the nose and throat.

clue.text: Singers right to raise serving-up of Australian spicy food

indicators.note: in a down entry raising a letter moves it higher, one place earlier

parts.note: a choir is a group of singers

indicators.note: serving-up in a down entry means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: Oz is informal for Australia or Australian

explanation.surface: A choir rightly honours an Australian cook dishing up spicy fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to raise' moves R up one place in CHOIR, giving CHORI; 'serving-up of' turns OZ into ZO.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy Spanish pork sausage flavoured with paprika is a spicy food.

clue.text: Droop over pudding

parts.note: to sag is to droop
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone slumps over a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk pudding made from starchy palm pearls is a traditional British school dessert.

clue.text: Get loose during sundown

indicators.note: during means within, so the letters are found inside the word sundown

explanation.surface: Breaking free as the sun goes down.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten or untie something is to let it come loose.

clue.text: Take pipe that's broken by second joint

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

indicators.note: the pipe is broken open by the second's letter going inside it

parts.note: an oat is a shepherd's pipe made of an oat straw

explanation.surface: Taking a pipe that has been broken in a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' is a cut of meat cooked in the oven, not a hinge or a smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sunday joint of meat is cooked in the oven, and also called this.

clue.text: Dressing needs first-class oil when mixed

parts.note: A1 means first-class, the 1 read as I

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of oil are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A salad dressing needs top-quality oil, well blended.
explanation.definitionFit: A garlic mayonnaise from Provence served as a sauce or dressing.

clue.text: Socialist coming from the south with very little fuel

indicators.note: in a down entry coming from the south means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist
V is the abbreviation for very, a little version of the word

explanation.surface: A left-winger arrives from the south with almost no petrol.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain it is the name for diesel oil used to power road vehicles.

clue.text: Rent meadow? That's a point

parts.note: a lea is a meadow in poetry
SE, south-east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Renting a meadow: is that the point of it?
explanation.definitionFit: To let or hire property for a fixed term is to rent it.

clue.text: Return journeys around island with large organisation, initially lively

indicators.note: around puts the reversed journeys round the island letter
return means the word for journeys is read backwards

parts.note: trips are journeys
OS is outsize, a large clothing size

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of organisation

explanation.surface: Planning return trips to an island with a big organisation, lively at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' turns TRIPS into SPIRT, with I placed inside to make SPIRIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction, Italian for spirited, telling players to perform with animation.

clue.text: Speak to upset heard with a vow

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone upset at having been heard making a vow.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to have a private talk with someone, often a reprimand.
